title: The Harvest of Old Chapel Road
premise: Lena Reyes, a nonbinary urban explorer who documents unmapped tunnels beneath the town of Harrow's Bend, discovers that the passages under Old Chapel Road were dug by her own great-grandfather as part of a bargain that traded the family's memory for protection. The house she inherited has been keeping something fed for four generations, and every mirror in it now reflects one second late because the thing inside is learning to imitate her. As the longest night of the year approaches, Lena must decide whether to complete the ritual that would bind the entity to another generation or break the inheritance entirely, knowing the price is her own remembered identity. She breaks the cycle at dawn, walking out of the house unable to recall her own name but free, leaving the mirrors reflecting nothing at all.
about_author: Ivo Voss is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping municipal infrastructure in New England before turning to horror. Their fiction explores what buildings remember about the families who pay their debts.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't There
chapters.summary: POV Lena. While mapping storm drains beneath Old Chapel Road, Lena finds a brick-lined tunnel absent from every county record, marked with her family name chiseled into the keystone. The emotional beat is professional curiosity curdling into unease when her compass spins only inside the tunnel.

chapters.title: Inheritance Paperwork
chapters.summary: POV Lena. A lawyer's letter reveals Lena inherited the house on Old Chapel Road from a great-grandmother she never knew existed. Exploring the sealed-up home, she finds four generations of identical journals, each ending mid-sentence. The beat is dread disguised as genealogy.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The bathroom mirror begins lagging: her reflection moves a full second behind. She tests it with a metronome, films it, and the footage shows nothing wrong. The beat is gaslit self-doubt; twelve years of rational explanations start failing her.

chapters.title: What the Journals Fed
chapters.summary: POV Lena, with journal excerpts. Reading backward through the generations, she learns each ancestor 'invited' something in during a hard winter, trading memories of a loved one for survival. The final journal belongs to her great-grandmother and names Lena by birth name she no longer uses.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Remembers
chapters.summary: POV alternating between Lena and elderly neighbor Ruth Calloway. Ruth, the last person who attended a funeral on Old Chapel Road, warns Lena not to answer anything that knocks after midnight. The beat is fragile alliance; Ruth remembers what the family paid, and pities her.

chapters.title: Tunnels Under the House
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The survey tunnel connects directly to the cellar. Descending with headlamps and chalk, Lena finds walls carved with thousands of names, hers appearing repeatedly, scratched out and rewritten. The beat is claustrophobic revelation: the house has been rehearsing her.

chapters.title: The Reflection Learns
chapters.summary: POV Lena. The mirror-lag shrinks to half a second, then zero, and the reflection starts smiling when she doesn't. It mouths words she can almost read. The beat is terror of replacement; the entity isn't haunting her, it's auditioning to be her.

chapters.title: Ruth's Last Night
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Ruth burns her own family's copy of the covenant papers and dies peacefully before dawn, freeing herself. Lena finds the ashes of the papers on Ruth's porch and understands escape is possible but costs everything remembered. The beat is grief braided with hope.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: POV Lena. On the winter solstice, the entity offers the ritual renewal: sign, forget someone, live safe. The reflection steps out of the glass wearing Lena's face and old name. Lena fights it through the house, using the journals' recorded memories as weapons against a thing built from forgotten ones. Climax: she chooses erasure over continuation.

chapters.title: Sunrise on Old Chapel Road
chapters.summary: POV Lena, fragmenting. At dawn the mirrors reflect empty rooms. Lena walks out carrying a single journal page she can't read, unable to recall her name but certain she chose this. A passing driver asks if she needs help; she says yes, which no ancestor ever did. The beat is bittersweet freedom: identity lost, selfhood kept.
